children: Occidental Petroleum said it agreed to a pair of long-term offtake agreements to pipe carbon dioxide from facilities in the Delaware Basin for use in its Permian Basin operations.

Under the terms of the deal, two companies will secure CO2 from third-party natural gas processing facilities to be shipped via pipeline from the Delaware Basin, which is located across eastern New Mexico and west Texas, to the Permian Basin, which is also located in those two states.
The two project developers will fund and build the necessary infrastructure, Occidental added.
The projects are subject to final investment decisions, Occidental said, adding it expects initial shipments in 2029.

The projects include the combined development of nearly 100 miles of new CO2 pipeline infrastructure in the Delaware Basin, which will connect to the existing pipeline network that supplies the Permian Basin, the company added. The pipelines are being designed with additional capacity to allow other sources of CO2 to interconnect in the future.
Occidental also said it is pursuing offtake from additional third-party sources of anthropogenic CO2.
Older oil wells can benefit from injections of CO2, which can reduce viscosity, restore pressure, and increase the amount of oil which can be recovered.
